https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/news/belfa.text: A delivery driver was threatened with a knife during an armed robbery in West Belfast over the weekend. At around 3.35pm on Saturday afternoon, September 12, a delivery driver was targeted in the Roumania Rise area at its junction with Servia Street. The driver had been delivering parcels and when he returned to his van, found three men standing at it with the rear door open. One of the men approached the driver with what is believed to have been a knife, while the other two men removed parcels from the vehicle. Following this, the three men fled the scene. Police have issued an appeal for information and witnesses of the incident to get in touch. Detective Sergeant Barnes said: “Police received a report that at approximately 3.35pm on Saturday afternoon, 12th September a delivery driver was targeted in the Roumania Rise area at its junction with Servia Street. “It’s reported the driver had been delivering parcels in the vicinity when he returned to his van to discover three men standing at it, and with the rear door open. “One of the men, dressed in a black tracksuit and with his face covered, approached the driver with an object – believed to be have been a knife – while the two other men removed a number of parcels from the vehicle. “All three men then fled the scene with the stolen goods – thankfully no injuries were reported. “This would have been a frightening experience for the driver - that happened at a time of day when people would have been going about their everyday business. “We’re appealing to anyone who was in the area at the time and saw any suspicious activity, or who might have any CCTV, dash-cam or other footage which could assist with enquiries, to get in touch. “You can contact us on the non-emergency number 101, quoting reference number 1177 12/09/26.” A report can be submitted online using the non-emergency reporting form via https://reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals . Or you can also contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or online at http://crimestoppers-uk.org/ . https://wwd.com/runway/spring-2027/paris.text: Business Looting and Unrest Mar Milan Protests, Retailers Hit Hard Fashion Bridal Fall 2027 Highlight: Sébastien Luke Business Jacob Cohën Opening First U.S. Store on Madison Avenue View Gallery 44 Photos View Gallery 44 Photos Mugler Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear Collection at Paris Fashion Week Dominique Maitre/WWD Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk This season’s Mugler show was all about the birds and the bees. Miguel Castro Freitas posted a trailer on Instagram that featured mating snails (try Googling “snail sex” — it’s actually fascinating) spliced with footage of two people exchanging saliva. It must be something in the air. From the couples making out at the Diesel show to the heavy breathing soundtrack at Tom Ford, designers are in the mood for, erm, love. The third installment of a trilogy, his “Naturalia X” collection delved into the flora and fauna inspirations present in the work of founder Manfred Thierry Mugler, who was a master at channeling savage beauty. You May Also Like Designs like a feather tunic resembling a butterfly wing, croc-embossed leather pants and a spider web dress all referenced Mugler’s seminal spring 1997 haute couture collection “Les Insectes.” “It’s looking into the feral aspect of nature versus the ethereal aspect of nature — the fragility versus the danger,” Freitas said backstage. Since joining the house last year the designer has steadily shaped a vision for Mugler rooted in hard-edged glamour. There was a futuristic sheen to his sculptural tailoring in gleaming Mikado silk, offset by the earthiness of faux fur pants and a snakeskin hourglass dress with cheeky bum cleavage. Freitas enlisted a team of specialists to work on couture-grade pieces including a shaggy hair tunic with a flame-colored motif, sweeping latex fringe evening gowns and molded leather dresses that sprouted strange flowers. Models walked through an immersive video installation by artist Casper Sejersen with an ear-splitting soundtrack by Teho Teardo. It featured a track by Björk, who wore a custom look from the collection for a DJ performance in Poland on the same day as the runway show. Adding to the unsettling ambience, front row guests included performance artist Alexis Stone in full prosthetic makeup, disguised as Manfred himself. He was seated next to the late designer’s husband Krzysztof Leon Dziemaszkiewicz. Beauty Gallery 20 Photos View Gallery “It’s quite surreal,” Freitas conceded. “We approached his husband to get his blessing. It was very important to know that he would be comfortable with seeing the image of the man that he shared his life with, sharing the same venue, and he was very entertained with the idea. He said that Manfred would have loved that.” Online reaction to the stunt was mixed, casting a shadow over a collection that could easily stand on its own merits. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6y4.text: Image source, Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images By Henry Moore Published 9 November 2026, 06:23 GMT Updated 2 hours ago A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say. The 24-year-old was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, and died early on Monday morning, police said. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. Officials initially reported the gunman had apparently been inspired by "far-right ideologies", but have since said they are still investigating any possible motivation. After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man. He has not yet been officially named. In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. However, during a press briefing on Monday morning, PrzemysÅaw Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, said investigations into his motive remain ongoing. Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack. Figure caption, People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. Four firearms were found in the gunman's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition, Nowak said. Authorities also seized at least four phones from his car and person, and electronic equipment from his home. Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. Speaking on Sunday, one of two surgeons who treated victims on the street after the attack said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer. The two surgeons, who were eating near the Main Market Square when the gunman opened fire, rushed to the scene to treat both the attacker and the two injured police officers. Figure caption, Watch: Doctor who treated victims of Krakow shooting speaks to the BBC Professor Michal PÄdziwiatr told the BBC: "We saw the shooting attack. And what a surgeon can do in a situation like this?... We decided to help the victims as soon as possible." "We rushed into the area where the shooting was and started our rescue, because there were no ambulances available, there were no professionals around." PÄdziwiatr said his colleague, who has been named by local media as Dr Mateusz Wierdak, used his hand to stem the bleeding from the most severely injured policeman, allowing time for an ambulance to arrive. On Sunday it was reported that both injured officers had emerged from comas. Witnesses who were near the Main Market Square have described their panic and confusion as the attack unfolded. Ruby, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives". She said they "just kept sprinting" until they found a hotel to shelter inside. Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover". "I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said. In the wake of the shooting, Poland declared the country would enter two days of national mourning. After travelling to Krakow, Tusk said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow." UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w". "My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added. Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted.
